title: Rain Slants? Relative Velocity Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
Stand still in the rain and it falls straight down. Run, and it seems to hit your face. Aarav cycles to college holding his umbrella straight up, and his shirt still gets wet in front. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (Chapter 3, Motion in a Plane; relative velocity in two dimensions is part of the JEE Main kinematics syllabus) we learn relative velocity in a plane.

A live simulation lets the rain fall at 5 m/s while Aarav speeds up to 5 m/s. Switch to his view and the drops slant toward him, while a graph of the slant angle climbs to 45°. A slow-mo replay flips his velocity arrow and adds it to the rain's. We find the rain he sees part by part, v_RA = v_R - v_A, its size 5√2 m/s and the angle tan θ = v_A / v_R, compare standing with riding, follow a boat across a river link by link and answer two pause-and-think questions. Then a worked river crossing, the exam trap of adding instead of subtracting, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Rain that seems to hit your face
0:28 What is relative velocity in two dimensions?
0:50 Live simulation: rain seen from the ground and from the bicycle
1:33 The angle, part by part: tan θ = v_A / v_R
2:22 Standing vs riding + pause and think
2:55 A boat crossing a river, link by link
3:37 Worked example: crossing a 100 m river
4:12 Exam trap: add or subtract?
4:35 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:19 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Force and Inertia, the first topic of Chapter 4. Flick a card out from under a coin, and the coin drops straight down. Why does it stay?
